result:
Rewrote `scenario.json` to remove the broken base-query elements.

What changed:
- Dropped the team (`teamId`→`teams.name`) and state (`stateId`→`workflow_states.name`) edges from the reference query. Since the DROP-subscriber mutant also matched nothing, one of those edges (or the `state` seed arg) was schema-wrong; both are gone from the query, and `state` is omitted from all seed issues (they take the documented `"Todo"` default).
- New anchors are facts-documented `issues` attribute filters: title contains "webhook" (A:Issue.title), description contains "rate limit" (A:Issue.description), priority == 2 (A:Issue.priority). New request: "Set the estimate to 8 on the high-priority webhook issue about rate limiting that Dana Whitfield is subscribed to."
- Re-titled/re-described all four candidate issues so target + all three decoys share the webhook title keyword and a "rate limit" description phrase; backgrounds ("Redesign billing settings page", "Rotate staging database credentials") fail 3 and 4 conditions respectively.
- Subscriber edge now uses snake_case association columns (`issue_id`, `user_id`) per the backend's junction-table convention (calendar `event_id`, `row`-op table names), keeping the same two-hop shape; F1 SUB replacements still use model-documented `assigneeId`/`creatorId`.

Decoys unchanged in design: @d1 F1 assignee Dana, @d2 F1 creator Dana, @d3 F0 subscriber Omar — each now fails only the subscriber condition against the new attribute base.
